items.description: Analyze repository structure and tool capabilities
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/repo_analysis.md documenting: (1) all modules in .archivara/ and .opencode/ with their purposes, (2) available tools (concept_evolve commands, semantic_scholar commands), (3) agent roles and permissions, (4) directory layout for results/concept_evolve/tree/. File must be ≥500 words.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive web and Semantic Scholar literature search on Bloch-type constants
items.acceptance_criteria: Search for at least 20 queries spanning: univalent Bloch constant bounds, Skinner 2009 method, Carroll Ortega-Cerda upper bound, Koebe covering theorems, Loewner chain extremal problems, variational methods for univalent functions, computer-assisted proofs in geometric function theory, and Bloch constant computability. Save raw search results to results/phase1/literature_search_log.md with timestamps and queries used.

items.description: Build citation graph for the univalent Bloch constant using Semantic Scholar and literature-graph-miner subagent
items.acceptance_criteria: Use semantic_scholar graph command seeded with Skinner 2009, Carroll & Ortega-Cerda 2009, Bhowmik & Sen 2023, Yanagihara 1995, Beller & Hummel 1985, and Baernstein & Vinson 1998. Delegate to literature-graph-miner subagent to identify cross-domain transferable ideas. Produce results/phase1/citation_graph.json with ≥30 nodes and results/phase1/transferable_ideas.md listing ≥5 cross-domain technique candidates.

items.description: Create and maintain sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib in repo root contains valid BibTeX entries for at least 15 relevant papers, including: Skinner 2009, Carroll & Ortega-Cerda 2009, Carroll 2008, Bhowmik & Sen 2023, Yanagihara 1995, Beller & Hummel 1985, Bonk Minda Yanagihara 1997, Baernstein & Vinson 1998, Rettinger 2008, Goodman 1945, de Branges 1985 (Bieberbach conjecture), Xiong 1998, Chen & Gauthier 1996, Pommerenke 1975 (Univalent Functions), and at least 1 additional paper discovered during literature search. Each entry must have author, title, journal/booktitle, year, and DOI/URL where available.

items.description: Synthesize precise mathematical problem statement with all known bounds, methods, and open questions
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase1/problem_synthesis.md containing: (1) rigorous definitions of B, B_l, L, B_u with the chain B ≤ B_l ≤ L ≤ B_u, (2) table of all known bounds with citations to sources.bib, (3) summary of Skinner's lower bound method (bootstrapping Koebe-type estimates), (4) summary of Carroll-Ortega-Cerda's upper bound method (harmonic symmetry, conformal welding, Goodman domains), (5) explicit list of ≥3 open sub-problems that could yield tighter bounds. Must cite at least 10 papers from sources.bib.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve 'evolve' to generate cross-domain concept tree for univalent Bloch constant improvement
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve evolve with topic 'Improving bounds on the univalent Bloch constant via variational methods, Loewner chains, coefficient estimates, and computational approaches'. Verify results/concept_evolve/tree/ contains index.json, adjacency.json, and walk_paths.json. At least 8 concept cards generated. Produce results/phase1/concept_tree_summary.md summarizing the top 5 most promising concept paths for bound improvement.

items.description: Implement numerical Koebe covering radius computation for univalent functions parameterized by Loewner driving functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Python script results/phase2/koebe_radius.py that: (1) represents univalent functions via truncated Loewner chains with piecewise-constant driving functions, (2) computes the conformal image f(D) for a given driving function using numerical ODE integration, (3) estimates the inradius (largest inscribed disk radius) of f(D) centered at any point, (4) includes unit tests verifying the identity map f(z)=z yields inradius=1 and the Koebe function yields inradius=1/4. Tests must pass.

items.description: Reproduce Skinner's lower bound B_u > 0.5708858 as baseline verification
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement Skinner's bootstrapping method in results/phase2/skinner_baseline.py. Script must: (1) implement the growth/distortion estimates used in Skinner 2009, (2) carry out the iterative improvement (implicit function bootstrapping), (3) output a numerical lower bound that matches 0.5708858 to at least 5 decimal places. Include detailed comments explaining each step with references to specific equations in Skinner 2009. Produce results/phase2/baseline_verification.md confirming reproduction.

items.description: Implement Carroll-Ortega-Cerda upper bound domain construction for baseline
items.acceptance_criteria: Python script results/phase2/upper_bound_baseline.py that: (1) constructs the threefold-symmetric Goodman-type domain from Carroll & Ortega-Cerda 2009, (2) computes the conformal map from D to this domain numerically (using e.g. Schwarz-Christoffel or BIE methods), (3) estimates the inradius ratio yielding an upper bound for B_u, (4) outputs a value ≤ 0.66 confirming their bound. Produce results/phase2/upper_bound_verification.md.

items.description: Delegate to concept-tree-explorer subagent to identify missing links and propose computational experiments
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent on the concept tree from item_006. Subagent must: (1) traverse all walk paths, (2) identify ≥3 missing links between concepts (e.g., Loewner chains ↔ interval arithmetic, coefficient bounds ↔ domain optimization), (3) propose ≥3 concrete computational experiments that could yield improved bounds. Results saved to results/phase2/concept_gaps_and_experiments.md.

items.description: Establish metrics framework for evaluating bound improvements
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase2/metrics.py that defines: (1) function to compute gap = upper_bound - lower_bound, (2) function to compute relative improvement over Skinner baseline, (3) function to verify a lower bound via interval arithmetic (using mpmath or similar), (4) JSON output schema for all experimental results. Create results/phase2/metrics_baseline.json recording current gap (0.6564 - 0.5708858 = 0.0855142) and baseline lower bound 0.5708858.

items.description: Develop improved lower bound via refined distortion estimates for the class S
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement results/phase3/improved_lower_bound.py that: (1) uses sharper coefficient estimates (de Branges theorem |a_n| ≤ n and known refinements for |a_3|, |a_4|) to improve the growth bound |f(z)| ≥ G(|z|) for f in S, (2) feeds these into Skinner's bootstrapping framework, (3) iterates until convergence, (4) outputs a lower bound strictly greater than 0.5708858. Document the mathematical derivation in results/phase3/lower_bound_derivation.md with full proofs and citations. If no improvement is achieved, document why with quantitative analysis of the bottleneck.

items.description: Investigate Loewner chain / optimal control approach to extremal univalent functions for B_u
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement results/phase3/loewner_extremal.py that: (1) parametrizes univalent functions via Loewner differential equation with driving function μ(t), (2) formulates the minimization of the image inradius as an optimal control problem, (3) uses numerical optimization (gradient descent or Pontryagin maximum principle discretization) over driving functions, (4) reports the minimum inradius found over ≥1000 candidate driving functions. Document the formulation in results/phase3/loewner_approach.md. Compare found minimum against 0.5708858.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve 'probe' on the specific bottleneck: closing the gap between Skinner lower bound and Carroll-Ortega-Cerda upper bound
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve probe with topic 'Closing the gap 0.5708858 < B_u ≤ 0.6564: what structural property of the extremal domain determines the true value?'. Output must include: (1) ≥5 forced concept bridges from different domains (optimization theory, spectral geometry, probability on domains), (2) ≥2 anomaly/paradox observations, (3) ≥3 concrete steering directions. Save to results/phase3/probe_bottleneck.md.

items.description: Explore improved upper bound via optimized domain families with higher-order symmetry
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement results/phase3/improved_upper_bound.py that: (1) generalizes the Carroll-Ortega-Cerda threefold-symmetric domain to k-fold symmetry for k=2,3,4,5,6, (2) for each symmetry order, numerically optimizes the domain parameters (arc positions, lengths) to minimize the ratio (inradius)/(derivative at origin), (3) reports the best upper bound found across all symmetry orders. If upper bound < 0.6564, document the improvement in results/phase3/upper_bound_improvement.md. If no improvement, document quantitative analysis of why threefold is optimal.

items.description: Develop computer-assisted rigorous lower bound using interval arithmetic
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement results/phase3/rigorous_lower_bound.py using mpmath or pyinterval that: (1) encodes Skinner's bootstrapping in interval arithmetic so all floating-point errors are tracked, (2) uses certified bounds on coefficients of univalent functions, (3) produces a machine-verified lower bound for B_u with a rigorous proof certificate. The certificate (results/phase3/proof_certificate.json) must include: all interval enclosures used, the chain of inequalities, and the final rigorous bound. The bound must be ≥ 0.5708858.

items.description: Delegate to literature-graph-miner to find transferable techniques from spectral geometry, extremal length theory, and conformal mapping optimization
items.acceptance_criteria: Use literature-graph-miner subagent to: (1) search citation graphs from Polya-Chebotarev problem papers, conformal welding papers, and extremal length theory, (2) identify ≥3 techniques from these fields not yet applied to the univalent Bloch constant, (3) for each technique, provide a concrete sketch of how it could yield improved bounds. Results saved to results/phase3/cross_domain_techniques.md with citations added to sources.bib (total now ≥20 entries).

items.description: Systematic numerical experiment: sweep over parametric families of univalent functions to map the B_f landscape
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement results/phase4/bf_landscape.py that: (1) generates ≥5000 univalent functions from diverse parametric families (Loewner chains with various driving functions, polynomial approximations to S, starlike/convex subfamilies), (2) computes B_f for each, (3) identifies the 10 functions with smallest B_f, (4) produces a histogram of B_f values saved as figures/bf_distribution.png, (5) saves all results to results/phase4/bf_landscape_results.json. The minimum B_f found must be documented and compared against 0.5708858.

items.description: Targeted optimization experiment: find near-extremal functions using gradient-based optimization over Loewner driving functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement results/phase4/extremal_search.py that: (1) discretizes the Loewner driving function into N=50,100,200 parameters, (2) uses scipy.optimize or PyTorch autograd to minimize B_f over these parameters, (3) runs optimization from ≥20 random initial conditions for each N, (4) reports the best (smallest) B_f found and the corresponding driving function, (5) saves optimization trajectories and final results to results/phase4/extremal_search_results.json. Include convergence plots saved to figures/optimization_convergence.png.

items.description: Run ConceptEvolve 'reframe' to find alternative problem formulations that may unlock new approaches
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute concept_evolve reframe with topic 'Minimizing the inradius of the image of univalent holomorphic functions on the disk'. Reframings must span ≥8 domains including: optimal transport, spectral theory, free boundary problems, stochastic processes (SLE), combinatorial optimization, information geometry, hyperbolic geometry, and machine learning. Save to results/phase4/reframings.md. Identify the single most promising reframing and describe a concrete experiment to test it.

items.description: Evaluate all novel bounds against baseline and prior work
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/phase4/evaluation_summary.md containing: (1) table comparing all lower bounds obtained (Skinner baseline, refined distortion, Loewner optimization, interval arithmetic) with columns for method, bound value, rigorous/heuristic flag, and runtime, (2) table comparing all upper bounds obtained (trivial, Carroll-Ortega-Cerda baseline, k-fold optimization) similarly, (3) the tightest gap achieved [best_lower, best_upper], (4) comparison against all bounds cited in sources.bib. If any bound improves on the state of the art, highlight it prominently.

items.description: Delegate to concept-tree-explorer to walk the evolved concept tree and validate experimental results against concept predictions
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to: (1) walk all paths in the concept tree with depth ≥3, (2) for each walk path, check whether the corresponding experiment was run and whether results align with concept predictions, (3) identify ≥2 unexplored high-value concept paths that could yield further improvements, (4) propose specific follow-up experiments. Save to results/phase4/concept_validation.md.

items.description: Write rigorous mathematical writeup of any improved bounds with complete proofs
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/main_result.md containing: (1) precise theorem statement(s) for any improved bound (lower or upper), (2) complete proof with all intermediate lemmas, (3) comparison with Skinner 2009 and Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009, (4) discussion of which step in the proof provides the improvement, (5) all citations referencing sources.bib. If no improvement over state-of-the-art was achieved, document the tightest bounds obtained, explain why each approach fell short, and identify the precise bottleneck preventing further progress. Must be ≥2000 words.

items.description: Create comprehensive figures and visualizations
items.acceptance_criteria: Generate and save to figures/: (1) bf_vs_parameters.png showing how B_f varies with driving function parameters, (2) extremal_domain.png showing the image domain of the near-extremal function found, (3) bound_history.png showing the historical progression of B_u bounds from 1945 to present including any new results, (4) concept_tree_visualization.png showing the concept tree with highlighted productive paths. All figures must have proper labels, legends, and captions documented in figures/figure_captions.md.

items.description: Final sources.bib validation and completeness check
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib contains ≥20 valid BibTeX entries. Every paper cited in any results/*.md file has a corresponding entry. Run a consistency check (automated or manual) confirming: (1) no duplicate entries, (2) all entries have required fields (author, title, year), (3) all DOIs are valid format, (4) entries cover the full scope: classical results (Bloch 1925, Landau 1929, Ahlfors-Grunsky 1937), modern bounds (Skinner, Carroll, Bhowmik-Sen), computational approaches (Rettinger), and any cross-domain techniques discovered. Save check results to results/phase5/bib_validation.md.

items.description: Produce final research report synthesizing all findings
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/phase5/final_report.md (≥3000 words) containing: (1) Executive summary with the single best lower and upper bounds achieved, (2) Literature review section citing ≥15 papers from sources.bib, (3) Methods section describing all approaches attempted, (4) Results section with quantitative comparisons against prior work, (5) Discussion of what worked, what didn't, and why, (6) Future directions section identifying ≥3 concrete next steps ranked by feasibility and expected impact, (7) Complete reference list. The report must honestly assess whether any state-of-the-art improvement was achieved.

items.description: Delegate to concept-tree-explorer for final concept tree assessment and future research roadmap
items.acceptance_criteria: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to perform a final traversal of the complete concept tree in results/concept_evolve/tree/. Subagent must: (1) score each concept path by realized value (did it lead to bound improvement?) on a 1-5 scale, (2) identify the top 3 unexplored paths most likely to yield breakthroughs, (3) estimate the difficulty and timeline for each. Save to results/phase5/concept_tree_final_assessment.md. This assessment must reference specific experimental results from Phase 4.
